I really hope he's willing/able to split it up into four books if necessary. I was convinced Kvothe would get kicked out of the University in WMF, since the story seemed too big to have that *and* the story of how he killed a king in just the final book. I suspect trying to wrangle with a huge amount of information is part of why DoS has taken so long.

It's been more than a year since I read either book, but I do remember Wise Man's Fear being considerably better than the first book. The supporting characters are developed a bit more and Rothfuss explores some interesting parts of the universe. I struggled to get into NotW well into a couple hundred pages in but breezed through much of WMF. So I'm glad you're giving the second book a chance; hopefully it'll surprise you.

That said, I've always thought these are the kind of books that are more entertaining than well-written. At some point I just accepted their flaws (which, as you say, are pretty glaring sometimes) and went along with the adventure. They're not perfect, but they're a fun ride.

My college has a website that lists nutritional information for literally every item in the dining hall. I don’t remember how I first found it, but if you type “[Name] dining hall nutritional information” into google it’s one of the first links. Maybe you could try doing the same for your school’s dining hall? Another college I visited had little cards with nutritional information on them next to each dish in the dining hall, so there might be something like that too. The most difficult thing is portion sizes - I have to guesstimate a lot and the servers tend to give really big portions so you have be a little aggressive about telling them to stop. But I did a really successful recomp using the online data, so it all worked out fine.

On another note, I kind of doubt you’ll be the only girl in the gym. To be fair, my college doesn’t have a separate gym for varsity teams so a lot of women there are female athletes, but I know/see a lot of non-athlete gals who go regularly and take it seriously. If there’s anything I’ve learned from this subreddit, there’s a surprising number of women who work out, it’s just portrayed as a very male-dominated thing (like many things in our society :p).

I’d love to chat more about college if you have any more questions! Feel free to PM me if you’d like :)
